2  ORDER
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

2. This is first bail application filed on behalf of the applicants under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of anticipatory bail relating to FIR/Crime No. 268/2023 dated (not mentioned), registered at Police Station-Suthaliya, District-Rajgarh (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 306/34 of IPC, 1860.
3 . The applicants are apprehending their arrest in the aforesaid crime, have knocked the portal of this Court for grant of anticipatory bail.
4. Allegation against the applicants is that due to torture by in-laws of the deceased by not sending his wife to deceased home, deceased Mahesh committed suicide.
5 . Learned counsel for the applicants submits that the applicants are innocent and have been falsely implicated in this offence.

The applicant-Laljiram happens to be father-in-law, applicant No.
2/Bhulibai happens to be mother-in- law who is a lady aged about 62 years, applicant No.
3/Mausambai-Sister-in-law and applicant No. 4/Raghuveer Singh happens to be brother-in-law of the deceased.

He further submits that the marriage between deceased Mahesh and Manisha was solemnized on 11.02.2023 and it is alleged that on the same day, the wife of the deceased went to her matrimonial home and after making efforts by the deceased and his father, she did not return back to her in-laws house.
On 12.07.2023, a complaint was lodged by wife of the deceased against her in-laws under Section 498A of I.P.C., owing to which, the deceased/Mahesh committed suicide.
There is no circumstantial evidence that the applicants have instigated or abetted the deceased to commit suicide.
Applicants are ready to co-operate with the investigation.
Final conclusion of the trial will take considerable long time.
Hence, he prays that the application of the applicants be allowed and they be granted the benefit of anticipatory bail.

6 . Learned counsel for the objector as well as Government Advocate submitted that due to false allegation of demand of dowry and cruelty made by wife of the deceased, the deceased/Mahesh committed suicide.
Therefore, no case is made out for anticipatory bail and hence prayed for rejection of the application.

7. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and looking to the facts and circumstances of the case and also age of the applicant No. 1 and 2, I am of the view that it is a case in which applicants may be released on anticipatory bail.
Consequently, this first application for anticipatory bail filed on behalf of applicants is hereby allowed.

The applicants shall comply with the following conditions:-
